data.why: the repo ships examples/sample_cscan.json, a C-scan JSON matching the documented schema, for the sidebar's C-scan file uploader

goals: configure a material preset, layup, panel size and impact energy, then run the empirical tier to get a quick residual-strength knockdown
compare empirical vs semi_analytical vs fe3d tiers on the same panel to see when delamination buckling or 3D first-ply failure changes the result
upload a C-scan JSON (inspection-driven path) instead of specifying an impact event, and get the residual strength from measured delamination ellipses
run a parametric energy sweep and export the knockdown-vs-energy curve as CSV
inspect the 3D damage mesh and damage-severity heatmap to see where delaminations and fiber breaks concentrate through the thickness
generate a nonconformance report (NCR) with a proposed MRB disposition from the analysis results

review.summary: The tree states BVID-FE's purpose well (residual strength after impact damage, from a modelled impact or a C-scan, at three fidelities, through to a proposed MRB disposition), and the cited screens support its numbers. It needs fixes before filing: the Knockdown Curve tab is described wrongly, tension and hand-entered specimen and impact settings are missing, the Buckling view is reduced to actions, and several feature cuts need adjusting.
